status_summary: The FTC is acting on children's online protection through COPPA and general Section 5 authority, but no proceeding built on the chapter's contracts-with-minors theory or a written parental consent requirement was found. The amended COPPA Rule was published 2025-04-22 and its full compliance date passed on 2026-04-22; the sources read describe no change to its under-13 scope, which the chapter criticizes. The FTC ordered seven companies on 2025-09-11 to report on AI companion chatbots and minors, and on 2025-09-29 referred a complaint against the Sendit app that includes a Section 5 unfairness count about pressuring children and teens into subscriptions. In 2026 the FTC held an age-verification workshop (2026-01-28) and issued a policy statement (2026-02-25) easing COPPA enforcement for data collected solely to verify age, which responds to the privacy concern the chapter's skeptics raise. On 2026-05-20 the FTC began enforcing the civil provisions of the TAKE IT DOWN Act, a related but distinct child-protection authority.

timeline.event: FTC publishes the amended Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule in the Federal Register (effective 2025-06-23; full compliance due 2026-04-22), adding separate parental consent for third-party disclosures, written security and retention requirements and coverage of biometric identifiers; the law-firm summaries read describe no change to the under-13 scope.

FTC issues Section 6(b) orders (vote 3-0) to Alphabet, Character Technologies, Instagram, Meta, OpenAI, Snap and xAI for information on how AI companion chatbots affect children and teens, including age restrictions, parental notice and COPPA compliance.

FTC (vote 3-0) refers to DOJ a complaint against Iconic Hearts Holdings, operator of the Sendit app, and its CEO, alleging COPPA violations (no parental notice or consent), deceptive practices, an unfairness claim over pressuring child and teen users to buy subscriptions, and subscription-billing violations; DOJ files in the Central District of California.
FTC holds a public workshop on age verification; Chairman Ferguson says he wants the COPPA Rule not to hinder effective age-verification technology (as summarized by a law-firm update).

FTC (vote 2-0) issues an enforcement policy statement under which it will not bring COPPA Rule actions against general-audience and mixed-audience operators that collect children's data solely to estimate age, without prior parental consent, if conditions on use, retention, sharing, notice, security and accuracy are met; it says it plans to review the COPPA Rule on age verification.
Compliance deadline for the amended COPPA Rule passes; FTC Commissioner Meador and a privacy division official said in March 2026 that children's protection is an enforcement priority.

FTC begins enforcing the platform notice-and-removal provisions (section 3) of the TAKE IT DOWN Act on nonconsensual intimate imagery, including AI-generated content, under which covered platforms must remove reported content within 48 hours; the week before, the Chairman sent reminder letters to four large technology companies. The act is adjacent to, not the same as, the chapter's unfair-contract theory.
